notification.title: By the way, you're in North Beach
notification.body: Columbus Avenue cuts diagonally through the old Italian quarter, and Washington Square is just up the road.

places.title: North Beach, San Francisco
places.snippet: Look up: you're in San Francisco's Little Italy. Columbus Avenue was cut through the neighbourhood and still lines up cafes, bakeries and bookshops.

places.title: Columbus Avenue
places.snippet: This diagonal street runs from the Financial District to Fisherman's Wharf, cutting across the city's regular grid.

notification.title: By the way, you're standing at City Lights
notification.body: Lawrence Ferlinghetti co-founded this bookstore-publisher in 1953. And the alley next to it is named after Jack Kerouac.

places.title: City Lights Bookstore
places.snippet: Look up: you're standing at the bookstore poet Lawrence Ferlinghetti co-founded in 1953. It's still a bookshop and a publisher, focused on world literature, the arts and progressive politics.

places.title: Jack Kerouac Alley
places.snippet: The alley beside the shop is named after the Beat writer who used to hang out at the pub and bookstore next to it. It links Chinatown's Grant Avenue with North Beach.

places.title: Vesuvio Cafe
places.snippet: Just across the alley is a historic bar, in a building Italian architect Italo Zanolini designed and built in 1913.

notification.title: By the way, you're at Portsmouth Square
notification.body: This plaza is where San Francisco began as a town, and today it's Chinatown's living room.

places.title: Portsmouth Square
places.snippet: Hard to believe, but this small plaza was the center of the village of Yerba Buena before it became San Francisco.

places.title: Chinatown, San Francisco
places.snippet: Look around: this is the oldest Chinatown in North America and one of the largest outside Asia.
